request.spec:
Show on each person their settled-total (the due of their SETTLED claims that count, at
their frozen figures, corrections included) and their open-total (the due of their OPEN and
PENDING claims that count: a held, deferred or retired-and-excluded claim is left out as it is
from the due-total). Show the sheet's settled-total and open-total too, each simply everyone's
figure added up (not trimmed). The two must add up to the person's untrimmed due-total before the
cap.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
Show on each person their settled-total (the due of their SETTLED claims that count, at
their frozen figures, corrections included) and their open-total (the due of their OPEN and
PENDING claims that count: a held, deferred or retired-and-excluded claim is left out as it is
from the due-total). Show the sheet's settled-total and open-total too, each simply everyone's
figure added up (not trimmed). The two must add up to the person's untrimmed due-total before the
cap.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
I've added the settled-total and open-total, for each person and for the sheet, and all 4 acceptance tests pass under `bin/e2e`.

The change is all in `src/main/frontend/src/app/features/people/people.ts`. The app already works out the due-total in the front end, so nothing changed on the server, in the stored data or in the audit file.

- **Each person:** each row has two new columns, "Settled due" (`person-settled-total`) and "Open due" (`person-open-total`).
  - The settled-total adds up the due on their SETTLED claims that count, using the figure frozen when each was settled, corrections included.
  - The open-total adds up the due on their OPEN and PENDING claims that count. A held, deferred or retired-and-excluded claim is left out, the same way the due-total leaves it out.
  - Both use the same list of claims as the due-total, so together they equal the due-total before the cap.
- **The sheet:** "Settled in total" (`rollup-settled-total`) and "Open in total" (`rollup-open-total`) appear next to the existing totals. Each is a plain sum over everyone, not trimmed like the sheet's due-total.

A claim with no figure (no rate to work from) adds nothing, so these totals show `0.00` where the due-total would show "n/a".
